ratings_why.fun: Setting the river each turn is a real decision, early Spawns now pay, and the late game has two different payoffs; the Stamp bookkeeping and the Warden trap keep it at 7.
ratings_why.distinct: Over a 7 because the fight itself moves your board: deaths pull the run up the zigzag and reaching F1 is the resource, which no current tribe or typical auto-battler tribe does.

verdict_why: The v2 fixes landed and nothing left is broken or unreadable; what remains are tuning ideas the owner can balance later.

points.text: Warden of the Hazel Well spends every fish that comes Home, so without Mother Redd a long cascade turns your best fish into Alevins. Letting only the first Spawn, with the rest giving just their Gift, would make it a direction card on its own.
Old Kelt with one gap gives a Stamp to the whole run and a homecoming every fight, so in spend builds he may be the default opener. Worth watching whether the lost slot is enough of a price.
Pebble-Carrying Hen is a Tier 4 whose output is about one Stamp per Spawn. It could also let the Alevin keep the Gift it would have caught, so it pays like a Tier 4.

The curve has a good shape: small positive Spawns early, Stamps compounding by Tier 4, then Redd, Bradán or Llyn Llyw as distinct finishes. Keep the Gift's tier term; it is what makes early homecomings worth taking.

standouts.why: Old Kelt turns one empty slot into a whole-run cascade at Start of Combat; the seed's image as a mechanic.
The Bailiff is both a Stamp engine and a Spawn-on-demand outlet, and the No Leap heron blocks the way home for the Long Road.
The Salmon of Llyn Llyw makes the never-go-home plan a real capstone and lets other tribes climb.

weakest.why: Pebble-Carrying Hen adds about one Stamp per Spawn, small for Tier 4.
Sea Trout Ferrywife only matters for other tribes' units, since Salmon already Leap.
Claw-Marked Cock is a solid but generic leap-for-stats body next to Kype.

flags.note: With the Warden, Mother Redd keeps every homecomer and makes a Gift each, around 4-5 times the Tier 6 guide a turn, plus Alevins toward a golden and a Discover; the hand limit is the only brake.
Old Bradán replays every Gift in fight, about twice the Tier 6 guide; golden doubles it. Not a loop, but hot.
Falls-Leaper counts every leap, and cascades pull up to six at once, so +15-20 Attack in fight at Tier 3 is plausible.
Without Mother Redd the Warden can spend most of your board in one turn; check that players don't read it as a trap.
